findings.summary: `git restore --staged` is treated as harmless when `"--worktree" not in rest and "W" not in shorts`. git's parse-options accepts unique prefixes of long options, so `git restore --staged --work f` (or `--worktr`) also discards working-tree changes. `_single_preview` lets that line through, and it skips the DELETE_RE text pass as well. Check prefixes of `--worktree` (any `--w…` that git would resolve to it), or ask on any unrecognised long option. Add a Ks row for `git restore --staged --work f`.

`_git_clean_dry` returns True on the first `-n` or `--dry-run`. git's OPT__DRY_RUN is a boolean that a later `--no-dry-run` resets, so `git clean -n --no-dry-run -fd` deletes and is now silent. `git worktree prune -n --no-dry-run` (line 527) has the same gap. Honour the last of `-n`, `--dry-run` and `--no-dry-run` (and its prefixes), and pin both forms as Ks ask rows.

`if name in protected` compares the ref name as written. On the owner's case-insensitive macOS file system, the loose-ref backend writes `git update-ref refs/heads/MAIN <sha>` to the same file as `refs/heads/main`, so the protected branch moves while the rule stays silent. This diff already reads guard-config paths in lower case for exactly this reason (guard_config_class). Compare `name.lower()` against the lower-cased protected set, and add a D1 row with `refs/heads/MAIN`.

Traceability: this row and line 136 (`git grep -n "\.pem" -- tools`) go from ask to silent. The fixture `git restore --staged main.py` moves from ask to allow, `gh pr merge` moves from allow to ask, and the eleven group C relaxations (K1–K11) cite decisions 3a, 3b, aa, ab, ad, af and ag. The diff adds no DECISIONS.md line, no docs/rules update and no version bump for guard 0.9.0. Every relaxation of a regulated check needs its decision line (what, why, what would change it) in the same change, or a link in the PR to where it is recorded.

Gaps in the new secret-store and cache tables, so the same secrets or caches stay silent in other spellings. (1) `aws configure get` matches only the bare `aws_secret_access_key` or `aws_session_token`, but the documented `profile.varname` form `aws configure get default.aws_secret_access_key` also prints the key. (2) `_kubectl_output` (line 911) misses `kubectl get secret app --template='{{.data.password}}'`, where kubectl infers go-template output without `-o`. (3) `_DELETE_ONLY_WITH` (line 403) misses `go clean -modcache=true`, which Go's flag package accepts.

`_GRAPHQL_TRACKER_RE = re.compile(r"Issue|Label")` denies only mutation fields that name an issue or a label. `addComment`, `addAssigneesToAssignable` and `removeAssigneesFromAssignable` on an issue id only ask, although their REST and CLI twins (`gh issue comment`, `POST …/issues/3/comments`) are denied (rows Ls). This is either a deliberate scope of decision aa, and then belongs in its DECISIONS.md line, or a gap.

summary: Guard 0.9.0 groups B and C: it widens the delete, deploy, secret-store, tracker and protected-branch tables, adds the unknown-wrapper net, reads GraphQL, and removes eleven kinds of false asks. The test loosenings that follow the relaxations come with the reason in a comment, and pinned rows show the harmful neighbours still ask, so none is a blocker. Two of the new 'harmless preview' carve-outs can be bypassed with git's own option parsing. The new update-ref deny does not cover the case-insensitive macOS file system that this same diff accounts for elsewhere. The diff records none of the relaxations in DECISIONS.md, the docs or a version bump.
